## 1. Purpose and scope
Archived reference implementation of the Solana validator and its surrounding Rust workspace. It implements a high-throughput, proof-of-stake blockchain node, client/CLI tooling, SDKs, built-in on-chain programs, local testing, and operational deployment utilities. The active successor is Agave, per `README.md`.

## 2. Primary entry points
- Validator process: `validator/src/main.rs`, with node bootstrap and operator CLI in `validator/src/bootstrap.rs` and `validator/src/cli.rs`.
- Local single-node validator: `validator/src/bin/solana-test-validator.rs`.
- User-facing command-line client: `cli/src/main.rs`, with command dispatch in `cli/src/cli.rs`.
- Genesis creation and ledger inspection: `genesis/src/main.rs`, `ledger-tool/src/main.rs`.
- Workspace composition and crate dependency boundaries: `Cargo.toml`.

## 3. Validator orchestration and network ingress
The validator composes transaction processing (TPU), validation/replay (TVU), gossip, RPC, persistence, and background services. Core lifecycle and service wiring reside in `core/src/validator.rs`; TPU and TVU pipelines are represented by `core/src/tpu.rs` and `core/src/tvu.rs`.

Inbound client transactions enter fetch/signature-verification/banking stages. `core/src/fetch_stage.rs`, `core/src/sigverify_stage.rs`, and `core/src/banking_stage.rs` form the principal execution ingress. Banking includes account-lock-aware, priority-based scheduling under `core/src/banking_stage/transaction_scheduler/prio_graph_scheduler.rs`.

Networking is split from consensus/execution: packet and QUIC/UDP transport are in `streamer/src/lib.rs` and `streamer/src/quic.rs`; cluster membership and CRDS gossip are in `gossip/src/cluster_info.rs` and `gossip/src/gossip_service.rs`.

## 4. Execution, state, and built-in programs
The runtime executes sanitized transactions against a `Bank`, applying fees, account changes, program invocation, and commitment state. Key boundaries are `runtime/src/bank.rs`, `svm/src/transaction_processor.rs`, and `program-runtime/src/invoke_context.rs`.

Persistent account state is owned by AccountsDB, which separates account caches, indexes, append-vector storage, hash verification, and snapshot-oriented persistence: `accounts-db/src/accounts_db.rs`, `accounts-db/src/accounts_index.rs`, and `accounts-db/src/append_vec.rs`.

Native programs define protocol-level instruction semantics, including system transfers, staking, voting, loaders, and address lookup tables: `programs/system/src/system_processor.rs`, `programs/stake/src/lib.rs`, and `programs/bpf_loader/src/lib.rs`. SBF program execution is an explicit sandbox boundary through loader syscalls and serialization.

## 5. Ledger, consensus, and block propagation
Ledger storage persists shreds, slot metadata, and blockstore state, then reconstructs/consumes blocks: `ledger/src/blockstore.rs`, `ledger/src/blockstore_processor.rs`, and `ledger/src/shred.rs`.

Proof of History services produce and record slot timing/entries via `poh/src/poh_service.rs` and `poh/src/poh_recorder.rs`. Leader output is shredded and propagated through Turbine broadcast/retransmission: `turbine/src/broadcast_stage.rs` and `turbine/src/retransmit_stage.rs`.

Replay validates ledger data into bank forks; consensus selects forks and tracks votes/tower state: `core/src/replay_stage.rs`, `core/src/consensus.rs`, and `core/src/consensus/heaviest_subtree_fork_choice.rs`. Repair services recover missing ledger data from peers under `core/src/repair/repair_service.rs`.

## 6. External-facing APIs and clients
RPC exposes account, transaction, subscription, health, and cluster views over the validator’s bank/ledger state: `rpc/src/rpc_service.rs`, `rpc/src/rpc.rs`, and `rpc/src/rpc_pubsub_service.rs`. Client libraries provide HTTP RPC plus direct TPU submission over QUIC/UDP: `rpc-client/src/rpc_client.rs`, `client/src/tpu_client.rs`, and `client/src/nonblocking/quic_client.rs`.

The public SDK defines transactions, messages, accounts, keys, signatures, and protocol data types shared across clients and nodes: `sdk/src/lib.rs`, `sdk/src/transaction/mod.rs`, and `sdk/program/src/lib.rs`.

## 7. Operations and infrastructure
Material runtime dependencies include Rust, native TLS/OpenSSL and protobuf tooling, optional GPU/performance libraries, disk-backed account and ledger storage, UDP/QUIC networking, and RocksDB-backed ledger components. Optional integrations include Google Cloud Bigtable archival access/upload through `storage-bigtable/src/bigtable.rs` and `ledger/src/bigtable_upload.rs`.

Metrics instrumentation is centralized in `metrics/src/lib.rs`; dashboards/scripts target InfluxDB and Grafana in `metrics/scripts/start.sh`. Cluster provisioning and remote-node operations support AWS, Azure, GCE, and colocation via `net/net.sh` and provider scripts under `net/scripts/`.
